Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied algebra and scheme results. Let R be a DVR, K its fraction field, k its residue field, and Rsh a chosen strict henselization. In clauses involving A, let A/K be the given abelian variety. An R-birational law on a smooth separated faithfully flat finite-type X over a DVR restricts to a strict law on an R-dense open U. Complete proof strategy: Intersect domains and images of universal translations, remove constructible bad-fibre-density loci in both projections, and intersect the two good opens. Restrict multiplication and use the open universal translations to verify both domain and image density in each projection. Source locators: BLR 5.2/2. In BLR 2.5/1(a), take the closed complement A of a quasi-compact open V in a smooth Y/S. Locally fix relative dimension d. The locus F in A where the A/S fibre has local dimension at least d is closed by exact `lem-local-fibre-dimension-bound-via-polynomial-quasifiniteness`; all these dimensions are at most d. A closed subset of an equidimensional smooth fibre has dimension d precisely when it contains a component, so V is not dense in that fibre exactly on the image of F. That image is constructible by `lem-finite-presentation-image-constructible`, covering F and the target by finitely many affine charts. This proves the density-locus assertion, without an unexamined EGA semicontinuity input.

Apply this with S=X and Y=X times_R X. The bad loci for each projection are constructible. They omit every generic point of both R-fibres because the original domain/image opens are R-dense. Over a DVR a constructible subset whose closure contained a fibre generic point would itself contain that generic point (a dense constructible set contains an open in its closure; use generization at the generic point). Therefore remove their closures and obtain an R-dense open good in both projections. The remaining strictification argument is exactly the read BLR 5.2/2 universal-translation argument. , use the smooth DVR total space explicitly. If a constructible bad locus omitted all generic points of the generic and special R-fibres but its closure contained a generic special point eta, an irreducible component of that closure containing eta has generic point q specializing to eta. The local ring at eta is a DVR, so the only possible q are eta and the total-space generic point. A constructible set dense in this irreducible closure component contains its generic point (published `lem-constructible-dense-contains-open`). Both possibilities contradict the stated omissions. Thus removal of the closure preserves fibre density. This is the exact dimension-one-base argument; it does not assert the analogous claim over an arbitrary base.

For the divisor-ampleness covering argument, the field-extension descent is also explicit. Given a closed point x in a fibre of G, put l=k(x), a finite extension of the fibre field k. On the geometrically integral (G0)l, the inverse images of the affine fibre-dense U under g to g x and g to g inverse x are nonempty opens, so their intersection W is dense open. The finite projection (G0)l to G0 takes its closed complement to a proper closed subset: the source is integral with the same-dimensional generic point, and that generic point is not in the complement. Remove this image to obtain a dense open Z over k; every g in Z(k) has both g x and g inverse x in U. The section-density argument above supplies such a section g of G0 over the strictly henselian DVR in either fibre. Therefore the section loci gU intersect g inverse U cover all closed points of each fibre. Every fibre point specializes to a closed fibre point and opens contain its generalizations, so they cover all of G. This supplies the “methods of descent” sentence in BLR 6.4/2 with a finite projection argument, including inseparable residue extensions.
 A strict law means that on an open U⊂X×_R X dense over each X projection the universal left and right translations are open immersions whose images are again dense over each projection. Thus pulling back by an arbitrary T-valued first or second coordinate yields a T-birational translation; universal schematic density supplies cancellation on arbitrary tests.
operations.after: Assume AC and DC. Let X be a smooth separated faithfully flat finite-type model over a DVR R with an R-birational group law and birational universal translations. There exists an R-dense model open Xzero inside X carrying a strict birational group law, with multiplication domain Uzero inside Xzero times Xzero and universal translations open immersions whose domains and images are dense over both projections. Xzero remains smooth separated faithfully flat finite type. In the commissioned abelian minimal-model case, the generic law is everywhere defined, so Xzero_K=X_K=A. Complete proof: form a common R-dense domain U of the universal translations and images V,W, and set Z=U intersect V intersect W. Its two bad-density loci in X are constructible and omit every fibre generic point. Separate their generic and special parts: the schematic closure of the generic part has a uniformizer-saturated ideal, which cannot be nonzero proper in a special height-one DVR local ring; the special constructible part has nondense closure by the dense-constructible-open lemma. Removing both closures gives the model open Xzero. Define Uzero=U intersect Xzero squared intersect m inverse Xzero. The original translation open immersions give density of its domain in each projection; for the remaining image densities, fix a output point a and use the two open immersions of m inverse(a) onto dense opens of X times a and a times X. This yields full both-projection density and cancellation on arbitrary tests by universal schematic density. This restores BLR 5.2/2, not a claim that arbitrary constructible closures over a DVR contain every special generic point they meet.
